The inbound topic allows custom prompts and hold music, a message when agents are unavailable, voicemail, and a forward to a third party. Those are different exits. Hold music is not voicemail. A forward leaves your agents entirely.
docs.eg: Third Party Transfer is an IVR module in the modules list. Voicemail Transfer is another. Picking the wrong one is a routing bug, not a carrier bug.

docs.ti: Priority and service level
docs.ex: Priority and service level. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The inbound topic says you can prioritize inbound traffic. Skill Transfer has a Priority tab in the community write-up. Skill groups themselves have service-level settings in the basic admin topic.
docs.eg: Priority is not the same number as a service-level target. One decides who gets the next agent when several calls wait. The other is how you measure whether the

docs.ti: Schedules, not a stopped campaign
docs.ex: Schedules, not a stopped campaign. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The campaign admin tree includes IVR script schedules for autodial and inbound campaigns. The planning topic tells you to set the campaign IVR schedule after the script exists. A schedule swaps treatment by time. Stopping the campaign does not. Stopping it returns busy.
docs.eg: This lab does not reproduce the schedule dialog field by field. Use the schedule when you need a night path, and confirm the campaign stays running.

docs.ti: Pause before the next call
docs.ex: Pause before the next call. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Skill Transfer has Pause Before Transfer, in seconds, on the General tab. The default is 0. A value above 0 waits that long after an agent is selected before the call is delivered, so a queue does not slap the next call down instantly.
docs.eg: The community article says those seconds do not show as On Hold in a report. On Plus applications the caller can sit in a Connecting state.

docs.ti: Inbound design review
docs.ex: Inbound design review. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A review you can finish in one sitting: DNIS, running campaign, script, skill on the Outbound Skills tab, overflow module, schedule, and pause. Each one has a public page. None of them is a trunk setting.
docs.eg: If all seven are right and the caller still hears silence or reorder, then you have a carrier or SBC symptom. The topology bench is the next tool, not another c

docs.ti: A list is not a campaign
docs.ex: A list is not a campaign. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Outbound and autodial campaigns dial lists of contact records. The list has an order. The campaign has a run state and a dialing mode. Uploading a CSV does neither of those.
docs.eg: The disposition topic says you reset list position and dispositions on the lists currently loaded in that campaign. A list sitting in the library and a list loa

docs.ti: Profiles filter the list the agent sees
docs.ex: Profiles filter the list the agent sees. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Campaign profiles filter and sort lists, control agent pop-ups, and manage disposition counts. They also override defaults such as the ANI. One campaign, one profile. Workflow rules can swap the profile.
docs.eg: A filter on the profile changes which rows are eligible. It does not change list penetration versus vertical. That choice is the list dialing mode on the campai

docs.ti: List penetration and vertical dialing
docs.ex: List penetration and vertical dialing. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. List penetration is the default. The dialer tries the first phone on every record, then the next phone on a later pass. Vertical dialing stays with one contact and moves across that contact's numbers before it moves on.
docs.eg: The community article's wording is easy to twist: it says the physical direction of list penetration is vertical, while the industry phrase vertical dialing mea

docs.ti: Reset is a loaded gun
docs.ex: Reset is a loaded gun. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Reset list position sends the dialer back to the top. Reset Disposition clears selected outcomes so those rows can dial again. Both act on lists currently loaded. The disposition topic says to reset only codes you know are safe.
docs.eg: A scheduled disposition update from CSV can also stamp codes, using a key field such as the phone column. The list details report is how you prove the stamp lan

docs.ti: Time zone and call analysis are guarded defaults
docs.ex: Time zone and call analysis are guarded defaults. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The campaign admin tree includes time zone dialing options, and the default-settings topic says call analysis and voice detection level ship with vendor defaults. Changing defaults can raise a compliance warning. The same topic says US domains watch abandon rate for 30 rolling days and UK domains for 24 hours, and that a Five9 representative sets which kind of domain you have.
docs.eg: This lab will not invent the legal calling window or the numeric abandon default. Both move, and both are jurisdiction-specific.

docs.ti: Call analysis is not a guarantee
docs.ex: Call analysis is not a guarantee. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Call analysis and voice detection level are defaulted campaign fields. Product pages also list answering-machine detection and automatic voicemail as agent-efficiency tools. None of those pages give you a percent accuracy you can put in a contract.
docs.eg: A live person marked as a machine is a silent failure: the agent never hears them, or a voicemail template talks to a human.

docs.ti: Local caller ID is a profile choice
docs.ex: Local caller ID is a profile choice. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The outbound product page lists local caller ID as a business-efficiency tool, and campaign profiles are the documented place to override the default ANI. Showing a local number is a profile and number-plan problem, not a skill-group problem.
docs.eg: Certified Caller, on its own page, is the STIR/SHAKEN story. A local ANI does not by itself mean the call is signed. Keep those projects separate.

docs.ti: Preview lets the agent read first
docs.ex: Preview lets the agent read first. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Preview delivers the contact and, on the product page, CRM history before the call is placed. It is the mode for conversations that need context. It does not overdial, so abandon from extra ringing lines is not the design.
docs.eg: The product page's Manual Touch mode goes further and removes automated dialing. Preview itself can still place the call after the agent has seen the record.

docs.ti: Progressive keeps one call per free agent
docs.ex: Progressive keeps one call per free agent. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The outbound product page says progressive dialing automatically dials one customer per available agent and is what centers use when they want to avoid dropped outbound calls. The dialer product page also says progressive is appropriate when fewer than 10 agents are active, and that it adapts pace to campaign performance.
docs.eg: Those two sentences are both public and they are not the same sentence. One says one call per available agent. The other says the pace adapts.

docs.ti: Power dials a ratio you chose
docs.ex: Power dials a ratio you chose. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The dialer page says power dials a user-configured number of calls per available agent and adjusts from abandon rates. It points that mode at a small group with a large list. The outbound page says the same shape: a small sales team and a large prospect list.
docs.eg: Because you choose the lines, you can create live answers with no agent. The abandon cap and the warning on the default-settings page are the brakes.

docs.ti: Predictive fills idle time, and it can drop calls
docs.ex: Predictive fills idle time, and it can drop calls. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The dialer page says predictive mode uses algorithms to predict agent availability and is suited to more than 10 active agents. The outbound page says it increases time spent talking to people instead of dialing. Both are marketing descriptions of an overdial.
docs.eg: The default-settings topic is the control room: monitor abandoned call percentage, a max percentage, a warning if you change the max, 30 rolling days on US doma

docs.ti: TCPA manual touch is a typed number
docs.ex: TCPA manual touch is a typed number. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. TCPA manual touch exists only on domains enabled for it. The community article says those domains are generally for telemarketing to cell phones without express consent, and that no other dialing mode is available. Contacts are shown and not dialed. The agent must type the external number. Paste and drag-and-drop are not allowed. The Dial button enables when the typed number matches.
docs.eg: Preview time still exists. If it expires, the agent goes Not Ready and nothing auto-dials. Dial Immediately and Dial Number are removed.

docs.ti: The defaults are the compliance posture
docs.ex: The defaults are the compliance posture. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. For every dialing mode, the default-settings topic says options start at values Five9 recommends for FCC, FTC, and UK Ofcom telemarketing rules. If you change them you can see a warning. The example field is Max Abandoned Call Percentage.
docs.eg: Other defaulted fields on that page include max queue time, the out-of-numbers alert, whether abandon percentage is monitored, call analysis, voice detection le

docs.ti: Pick a mode in one page
docs.ex: Pick a mode in one page. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Use the person's job, not the logo. Context before the call is preview. A promise of no dropped calls and a small team is progressive. A small team and a huge list, with eyes on abandon, is power. A large team whose idle time is the enemy is predictive, with dedicated agents. A cell book without consent is TCPA manual touch, and only if the domain is enabled.
docs.eg: The ten-agent lines on the dialer page are guidance from a product page. The abandon windows are admin-guide facts. The simulator is a classroom.

docs.ti: Blended is a staffing plan
docs.ex: Blended is a staffing plan. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The outbound product page says outbound works with inbound digital channels and that blended behavior lets agents move between inbound and outbound as inbound rises and falls. It does not add a campaign type named Blended to the planning roadmap.
docs.eg: You blend by which skills an agent holds and which campaigns are running, not by a secret fourth object. If inbound and a predictive book share the same people,

docs.ti: Autodial is the IVR's outbound
docs.ex: Autodial is the IVR's outbound. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Autodial is the third campaign type. The planning topic groups it with inbound when it tells you to record prompts and build IVR scripts. It still uses lists, like outbound. Think of it as the dialer reaching a person and then handing them a script, not an agent, unless the script transfers.
docs.eg: Skill assignment for autodial uses the same oddly named tab as inbound: Outbound Skills. An autodial campaign that is not running will not place those calls.

docs.ti: Priority and ratio are campaign settings
docs.ex: Priority and ratio are campaign settings. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The campaign admin tree includes a topic for campaign priority and ratio settings. This lab has not quoted that topic's fields, so it will not invent the numbers. What is safe to say is that inbound priority, Skill Transfer priority, and any campaign ratio are different screens until you have read them.
docs.eg: A blend fails when every campaign is 'the important one.' Write the order down: which campaign may steal an agent, and which may not.

docs.ti: Not Ready is a real state
docs.ex: Not Ready is a real state. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Agents are not always available. TCPA manual touch forces Not Ready when preview time runs out, and it does not dial. A blend that assumes every login is a dialer resource will over-predict.
docs.eg: Reason codes and Not Ready are how you explain the gap. They are not a carrier outage. Reports in the agent category are where you see the pattern before you ad

docs.ti: After-call work feeds the next dial
docs.ex: After-call work feeds the next dial. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A disposition is what the dialer remembers. A final code stops the record. A retryable code brings it back after the redial rules. Wrap time, in the simulator, is the gap before the agent is free again. Five9's pause-before-transfer is a different gap, on the next inbound delivery, and it is not reported as hold.
docs.eg: If wrap is fiction and pause is zero, a blended agent finishes one call and is instantly eligible. That is how a progressive book and an inbound queue trade the

docs.ti: Digital and voice share the person
docs.ex: Digital and voice share the person. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The outbound page says the dialer works with inbound digital engagement, and Agent Desktop Plus is the screen where voice, digital, and context are meant to meet. A blend that is only a voice story misses chat and email sitting on the same login.
docs.eg: Antivirus products can block digital text from loading. The technical requirements name that failure. A 'blend' that cannot show the chat is a desktop failure,

docs.ti: A blend you can defend
docs.ex: A blend you can defend. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A defensible blend is a paragraph: which campaigns run, which skills overlap, which mode each outbound book uses, who may be stolen, what Not Ready does to the count, and which abandon window the domain uses. Every noun in that paragraph is a screen you can open.
docs.eg: If you cannot point at the screen, it is not a design. The simulator can illustrate it. It cannot be attached to the domain.

docs.ti: The module list is the vocabulary
docs.ex: The module list is the vocabulary. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The IVR modules chapter names the blocks you may place. The list includes Play, Menu, Get Digits, Input, Voice Input, If/Else, Case, Set Variable, Lookup Contact Record, Query, Skill Transfer, IVA Transfer, Voicemail Transfer, Set DNC, Third Party Transfer, Foreign Script, Language, and others such as Conference, Iterator, and the Salesforce modules.
docs.eg: This lab's builder uses those names. It does not contain a module called Hangup, because that name is not in the chapter list this lab read.

docs.ti: Play, Menu, digits, and voice
docs.ex: Play, Menu, digits, and voice. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Play speaks a prompt or TTS. Menu takes a choice and has an exit per option. Get Digits and Input collect what the caller types. Voice Input and the Natural Language Processing module are the speech-side blocks in the same chapter. Input is what the ZIP-code web-service example uses, storing ZIP as a variable.
docs.eg: A menu that has no No Match path strands people who press the wrong key. Draw that exit before you draw option 1.

docs.ti: If/Else is two ways. Case is more
docs.ex: If/Else is two ways. Case is more. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. If/Else has two branches. The modules chapter includes both If/Else and Case. When you need three or more outcomes, Case is the block that exists for that. Nesting If/Else until the drawing looks like a hedge is how scripts become unreviewable.
docs.eg: The condition is your expression: open hours, a variable, a lookup result. The module does not know your business. It evaluates what you typed.

docs.ti: Skill Transfer has more than a skill name
docs.ex: Skill Transfer has more than a skill name. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The community article lists General, Skills, Announcement, Priority, Connectors, Queue Callback, and Disposition. It also says 'six tabs' and then names more than six. Count the tabs in your editor. Do not trust the word six.
docs.eg: Multiple skills mean any agent who has one of them may get the call. The article says Five9 recommends one skill in the module if you want useful reports.

docs.ti: Variables, lookup, and query
docs.ex: Variables, lookup, and query. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Set Variable writes a value. Lookup Contact Record reads the contact. Query calls out, and the published example is an XML web service POST whose response groups are mapped with regular expressions into variables. That example uses script variables, not call variables, because the caller is not connected to an agent.
docs.eg: Call variables are a different object, used when you need reporting later. Enabling them does not backfill history. A Query result you never store in a reportin

docs.ti: IVA, foreign scripts, DNC, and leaving the platform
docs.ex: IVA, foreign scripts, DNC, and leaving the platform. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. IVA Transfer hands the call to a Studio task. Foreign Script jumps to another IVR script. Set DNC is the removal action. Third Party Transfer leaves your agents. Language switches prompt language. These are five different exits. A diagram that says 'send to bot' does not say which one.
docs.eg: Digital IVA integration, in the March 2026 Studio article, needs a Studio API key with Build permission and a ChatBot task key pasted into the VCC side.

docs.ti: Visual IVR and frames
docs.ex: Visual IVR and frames. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The technical requirements say administrators can apply web page security so a Visual IVR script is not embedded in a frame where the user can be hijacked. The mechanism named is the X-Frame-Options header. The browser table in that PDF lists old versions and tells you to test others.
docs.eg: A visual script is still a script: prompts, branches, and a handoff. Framing is an extra threat. Do not treat a 2016-era browser row as the current support list

docs.ti: A skill is a queue with people in it
docs.ex: A skill is a queue with people in it. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A skill group holds users who have the agent or supervisor role. Campaigns point at one or more groups. The people, not the name, determine who can receive the contact.
docs.eg: Service level, voicemail, greetings, and a message to the group are all on the skill topic. A skill with no members is a label.

docs.ti: The tab is named backwards on inbound
docs.ex: The tab is named backwards on inbound. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Outbound campaigns take skills on the Skills tab. Inbound and autodial take them on a tab named Outbound Skills. The skill topic says this in one paragraph. People miss it because the word outbound sits on an inbound campaign.
docs.eg: If the right people are Ready and the queue is still empty, look at the tab before you look at the carrier.

docs.ti: One module, one skill, when you need the truth
docs.ex: One module, one skill, when you need the truth. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Skill Transfer may list several skills, and any agent who has one of them can take the call. The same article recommends a single skill in the module when you want reports that mean something.
docs.eg: A shared pool is a valid design. An accidental shared pool is how billing calls show up as a blob. Split modules if the work is different.

docs.ti: Skill level versus list order
docs.ex: Skill level versus list order. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The skill transfer article describes an option to ignore the order of skills in the module and distribute by the agent's skill level instead. Order and level are different ideas. Order is the list you typed. Level is a property of the agent.
docs.eg: This lab does not quote the click-path for editing an agent's level. If you use the option, confirm in the editor which number wins.

docs.ti: Default is a queue, not a compliment
docs.ex: Default is a queue, not a compliment. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. If Skill Transfer has no skill selected, the article says calls go to users who are not assigned skills. That queue is labeled Default in the softphone. It is a catch-all, not a place you want billing calls.
docs.eg: Supervisors and agents with empty skill lists become the Default pool. An empty list is easy to create when a user profile is cloned and skills are forgotten.

docs.ti: Service level is the scoreboard
docs.ex: Service level is the scoreboard. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The skill topic includes service levels. A service level answers 'how fast is acceptable,' usually as a percent of contacts answered inside a number of seconds. It does not, by itself, reorder the queue. Priority does the ordering. The scoreboard tells you if the ordering and the staffing worked.
docs.eg: A blend that steals agents will miss the inbound service level even when the skill is configured perfectly. The scoreboard is how you prove the steal rule.

docs.ti: Skill voicemail is its own mailbox
docs.ex: Skill voicemail is its own mailbox. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The skill topic covers routing voicemail to the group, greetings, messages, and audio files. That mailbox is not the campaign Play prompt and not an agent's personal phone mailbox unless you have built it that way.
docs.eg: Queue callback, on Skill Transfer, is yet another path, with its own disposition advice: the article says the default disposition is Abandon and tells you to cr

docs.ti: One screen is the product
docs.ex: One screen is the product. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Agent Desktop Plus is described as a single screen so the agent can stay with the customer. The Engage page adds real-time transcription, AI Agent Assist, and case context on that screen. The same underlying technology is what the desktop page says you get from Plus or from a pre-built CRM adapter.
docs.eg: A design that needs five browser tabs is the problem Plus is published to remove. If your floor still alt-tabs, you have not deployed the product you named.

docs.ti: Plus adapters speak HTTPS and WSS
docs.ex: Plus adapters speak HTTPS and WSS. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The technical requirements say Plus adapters use HTTPS and Secure WebSocket. If a proxy is in the path, it must support WSS. The PDF also says Five9 does not support TLS 1.1, and that browsers need TLS 1.2. Unencrypted API connections are refused.
docs.eg: A screen pop that fails while voice still works is often this path: the media is fine and the websocket is not. Do not replace the headset first.

docs.ti: Transcription and assist are features you turn on
docs.ex: Transcription and assist are features you turn on. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The Engage page describes transcription, sentiment language, and Agent Assist suggestions on the desktop. GenAI Studio's page says it powers Five9 AI applications and initially focuses on Agent Assist summaries, with control over the output.
docs.eg: None of those pages name a single model you can assume is the default in every domain. If a design says 'it uses model X,' mark that sentence uncertain until th

docs.ti: WEM lives in the same desktop
docs.ex: WEM lives in the same desktop. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The desktop page says Plus can show schedules, adherence, time-off requests, and evaluations without another app. CRM connectors can surface the same WFO actions inside Salesforce and the other named CRMs.
docs.eg: That is the staffing blend meeting the person: the agent can see that they are supposed to be on a break. A dialer that ignores the schedule will call it idle t

docs.ti: Digital text can be blocked
docs.ex: Digital text can be blocked. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The technical requirements say some antivirus software, naming Avast as an example, can stop chat, social, or email text from loading. Voice can continue. The symptom is a blank digital pane, not a busy DNIS.
docs.eg: Efficiency Mode can also sleep a background tab and drop a live call. Digital and voice fail differently. Write the symptom before you pick the cause.

docs.ti: Headsets and the path under the desk
docs.ex: Headsets and the path under the desk. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. USB noise-canceling headsets are the recommendation. Analog is not supported. Wireless is discouraged above about ten active agents because of delay. Wired LAN is preferred. Wi-Fi is tolerated only when bandwidth holds. Satellite and cellular, including 5G, are not supported.
docs.eg: Agent Desktop Plus and the adapters are listed at 128 kbps for G.711, which the PDF says is the default codec. Agent Assist adds 12 kbps.

docs.ti: The desktop review
docs.ex: The desktop review. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A desktop review is short: one screen, WSS through the proxy, TLS 1.2, the schedule visible, text not blocked, USB headset, supported path, Efficiency Mode off, and the bandwidth rows added up. Each line is from the product page or the PDF.
docs.eg: If those pass and audio is still one-way, you are in NAT and firewall territory, which is the SIP track. The desktop is no longer the prime suspect.

docs.ti: Five9 WEM and a Verint path both exist
docs.ex: Five9 WEM and a Verint path both exist. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The workforce page says Five9 offers WEM natively and also partners with vendors such as Verint so a customer can fit the suite they already run. It says Five9 manages installation, configuration, maintenance, and upgrades for the WEM solution they deliver.
docs.eg: Do not tell a floor they are 'on Verint' or 'on native WEM' without looking. The page says both exist. Recording, QM, analytics, WFM, surveys, and CRM connector

docs.ti: Workforce management is the roster
docs.ex: Workforce management is the roster. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. WFM, in the product language, is how you staff to the work: schedules, intraday changes, adherence. It is not the dialer mode and not the service level target, though it exists so those can be met.
docs.eg: A predictive book that uses headcount instead of the schedule will overdial at every planned break. The roster is an input to the mode you already chose.

docs.ti: Quality management listens on purpose
docs.ex: Quality management listens on purpose. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The product page describes multi-channel evaluations, desktop monitoring, and automated scoring. The desktop page says agents can review evaluations without leaving Plus. That is QM: a sample of work, a score, a conversation with the person.
docs.eg: A 100 percent score on a form nobody respects is not quality. The form has to match the call the customer had. Recording is the evidence.

docs.ti: Analytics and surveys sit beside the call
docs.ex: Analytics and surveys sit beside the call. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The data sheet and the product page put interaction analytics and customer surveys next to QM and WFM. Analytics is how you see topics across many calls. A survey is how the customer scores the one call. They are not the abandon rate and they are not a disposition, unless you deliberately map them.
docs.eg: This lab does not claim a specific analytics vendor screen. Native WEM and a partner suite will not look identical. The question to ask is which topics you will

docs.ti: Recordings expire
docs.ex: Recordings expire. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The retention page says VCC audio recordings are kept for the sooner of 30 days or a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or as the contract says. E911 call recordings are listed at 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. Disabled domains are listed at 120 days after closure. DIDs and toll-free numbers are listed at 90 days after closure.
docs.eg: If you need a call from last quarter, the offload had to succeed. A failed SFTP job is a silent deletion clock. QM cannot score what is already gone.

docs.ti: The agent should not need a second login
docs.ex: The agent should not need a second login. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The desktop page's point is that schedules, adherence, time off, shift bidding, and evaluations are reachable in Plus and, through connectors, in the CRM. A second password for WEM is a design smell if the connector was in the contract.
docs.eg: Shift bidding is named on that page. This lab does not reproduce the bidding rules. If bidding exists, the result still has to become the schedule the dialer re

docs.ti: What this lab will not pretend to run
docs.ex: What this lab will not pretend to run. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. This lab has no live WEM tenant. You cannot approve a real time-off request here. You can say which product page promised the button, which retention clock will delete the evidence, and which dialer mistake a bad roster causes.
docs.eg: That is the useful line between a simulator and a system of record. The pacing bench is a classroom. The schedule in the customer's suite is the roster.

docs.ti: Studio has regions
docs.ex: Studio has regions. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The technical requirements publish Studio portal hosts by region: five9.us, five9.au, five9.ca, five9.uk, and five9.br studioportal.io, plus older inferencecommunications.com names. A task built in the wrong region will not be the task your VCC domain can call.
docs.eg: SIP notes in that same part of the PDF, including UDP 5060 and a beta TCP 5061, are labeled next to Studio SBC material. Do not paste those ports onto every VCC

docs.ti: A task key is not a vibe
docs.ex: A task key is not a vibe. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. IVA Transfer is a module. It needs a task to transfer to. The digital integration article, dated in the community as 26 March 2026, says you copy a ChatBot task key into the VCC IVA transfer side after the Studio task exists.
docs.eg: Voice and digital write-ups are separate. Use the article that matches the channel. A key with no Build permission, in that digital article, is not enough: the

docs.ti: Contain, or hand back with context
docs.ex: Contain, or hand back with context. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A useful bot either finishes the job or returns the caller to a skill with the reason intact. IVA Transfer that dead-ends, or a Skill Transfer with no skill, is how you manufacture the Default queue.
docs.eg: The Engage page describes sentiment and a handoff to a human with context. Treat that as the product story. The variables you actually pass are the ones you sto

docs.ti: GenAI Studio is a hub, not a slogan
docs.ex: GenAI Studio is a hub, not a slogan. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The GenAI Studio page describes a low-code hub: choose among models, attach knowledge and customer data, test on real call data, keep a prompt library, and control output. It says the hub powers Five9 AI applications and initially focuses on Agent Assist summaries.
docs.eg: Engine-agnostic means you do not get to write a single model name into an architecture slide until the hub shows it. Responsible AI, on that page, is part of th

docs.ti: NLP in the IVR is not the same as Studio
docs.ex: NLP in the IVR is not the same as Studio. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The modules chapter includes a Natural Language Processing module and Voice Input, and it also includes IVA Transfer. They are different blocks. NLP inside a script is not automatically a Studio task, and a Studio task is not automatically the NLP module.
docs.eg: Pick the block that matches the design. If the work is a Studio bot with a task key, use IVA Transfer and the Studio article.

docs.ex: A bot review you can finish. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ti: ServiceNow releases are named
docs.ex: ServiceNow releases are named. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The same PDF says the ServiceNow Plus adapter supports the Service Operations and Configurable workspaces, and names the Australia, Zurich, and Yokohama releases. docs.ti: The rest of the named CRMs
docs.ex: The rest of the named CRMs. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Dynamics 365, Zendesk, Oracle, NetSuite, and Epic are in the same Plus adapter list as Salesforce and ServiceNow. The PDF does not give this lab a package number for each of them. docs.ti: SDK and connectors when there is no adapter
docs.ex: SDK and connectors when there is no adapter. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The desktop page says bring your own CRM with the SDK.

docs.ti: Screen pop down, voice up
docs.ex: Screen pop down, voice up. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. This is the signature adapter incident. The caller is heard. The record is not on screen. Causes you can cite: WSS blocked, TLS 1.1, the wrong CRM chapter, an unassigned campaign profile that was supposed to control pop-up behavior, or a connector pointed at a dead URL.

docs.ti: Salesforce modules inside the IVR
docs.ex: Salesforce modules inside the IVR. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ti: Three ways a call can enter
docs.ex: Three ways a call can enter. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The technical requirements describe three SIP stories. Five9 can provide ITSP trunks. Your ITSP can connect to Five9 session border controllers, and there is a checklist for that. Or a gateway you already own — Avaya, Cisco, or Asterisk — can talk to Five9 over the internet, a VPN, or Direct Connect.
docs.eg: Cisco in that sentence is a gateway type, not a promise that a UCCX script will import. Pick the story before you draw a codec or a DNIS.

docs.ti: DNS, codecs, and the default voice
docs.ex: DNS, codecs, and the default voice. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The requirements prefer DNS SRV for the SIP targets. G.711 is the default codec, and the PDF describes it as uncompressed. Do not invent a packetization time. A 20 millisecond ptime shows up in practitioner notes about Cisco gateways. It is not a number this lab will attribute to the Five9 PDF.
docs.eg: RFC 3261 is the SIP signaling baseline. RFC 4733 is the telephone-event way digits often ride once the call is up. DTMF design is a separate sentence from the c

docs.ti: How much bandwidth a seat costs
docs.ex: How much bandwidth a seat costs. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The requirements give planning numbers. Agent Desktop Plus and the Plus adapters are 128 kbps. The Java agent is 88 kbps. Agent Assist adds about 12 kbps. A VPN adds about 64. CRM or other business apps add about 64. A UC client such as Teams, Zoom, Office@Hand, RingCentral, or Nextiva is called out around 320 kbps.
docs.eg: One-way latency should stay under 150 ms. Wi-Fi is acceptable when the bandwidth is actually there. Wired is preferred. Satellite is not supported.

docs.ti: NAT, idle timers, and split tunnels
docs.ex: NAT, idle timers, and split tunnels. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. NAT and PAT are acceptable. Double NAT is not. UDP bindings that idle out cause one-way audio. The requirements use a 30 second UDP idle timeout as the planning number, and they tell you to send keepalives when the binding is shorter.
docs.eg: On a VPN, translate RFC 1918 space to a public address the far side can route. Do not exclude Five9 domains from a split tunnel and then wonder why signaling di

docs.ti: Direct Connect and the edges
docs.ex: Direct Connect and the edges. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Direct Connect in the requirements is a Layer-3 handoff. There is no Layer-2 requirement. The port is 10, 100, or 1000 full duplex, and failover uses BGP. Equinix Fabric edges named in the PDF this lab read are Chicago CH3, Washington DC10, London LD5, Amsterdam AM4, Frankfurt FR8, São Paulo SP4, Tokyo TY11, and Sydney SY5.
docs.eg: Those city codes are a snapshot. A new PDF can add or retire an edge. Write the date next to the list before a circuit is ordered.

docs.ti: TLS, and ports that are not universal
docs.ex: TLS, and ports that are not universal. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Unencrypted APIs are not the story. TLS 1.2 is required. TLS 1.1 is not supported. The requirements also list TLS 1.3 inbound ciphers: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, and CHACHA20.
docs.eg: Studio portal hosts and Studio SIP ports live in the Studio section of that PDF: UDP 5060, TCP 5061 described as beta, proxy UDP 5189 and TCP 5161, a legacy UDP

docs.ti: Headsets, and the call that only fails one way
docs.ex: Headsets, and the call that only fails one way. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. USB noise-canceling headsets are the recommendation. Analog headsets are not supported. Wireless is not recommended once you are above roughly ten agents. Windows 11 Efficiency Mode can drop live calls. Java admin is not the Mac ARM path; use the web admin there. None of that is a SIP trunk, and all of it still stops a call.

docs.ti: The API names on the product page

docs.ti: Call variables are not history
docs.ex: Call variables are not history. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ti: Prebuilt UC and the connector that is not an adapter
docs.ex: Prebuilt UC and the connector that is not an adapter. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ex: What an extract is allowed to remember. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Reporting Web Services can move numbers out of the domain. Retention still applies to what Five9 keeps, not to the warehouse you built. Once a row is in your bucket, your policy owns it.

A headquarters address while the agent is at home is the failure the EULA describes. Remote and hybrid floors have to register the location the agent is actually using.

docs.ex: Recording is the customer's duty too. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The EULA treats recordings as customer data. It says calls can be recorded while the caller is on hold and after a transfer. It puts notice and consent on the customer, who has to follow the laws that apply to their calls.

docs.ti: Retention is several clocks
docs.ex: Retention is several clocks. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. The public retention page splits the clocks. VCC audio is the sooner of 30 days, a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or the contract. E911 recordings are 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. A disabled domain is 120 days after closure. DIDs and toll-free numbers are 90 days after closure.
docs.eg: Quote the line that matches the object. 'We keep everything 30 days' is already wrong.

docs.ti: Attestation is not an ANI field
docs.ex: Attestation is not an ANI field. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Certified Caller is Five9's published STIR/SHAKEN program, tied to FCC and CRTC expectations. docs.eg: Say 'we set local ANI' or 'we are in Certified Caller.' If you cannot point at the Certified Caller page for the second sentence, do not say it.

docs.ti: Abandon rate is a regulated posture
docs.ex: Abandon rate is a regulated posture. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Default campaign settings call out a warning if you change Max Abandoned Call Percentage. Other fields on that page include Max Queue Time, Show Out of Numbers Alert, Monitor Abandoned Call Percentage, Call Analysis, Voice Detection level, and Action on Max Queue Time Expiration.

docs.ti: TCPA manual touch is a physical control
docs.ex: TCPA manual touch is a physical control. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. On domains where TCPA manual touch is enabled, other dialing modes are not available. Agents type the external number. Paste and drag are blocked. Dial enables only when the typed number matches. If preview times out, the agent goes Not Ready and nothing auto-dials.

docs.ex: The domain has neighbors. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. A Five9 domain does not live alone. Voice arrives on a SIP story. Agents sit in a desktop. WEM or a partner workforce suite watches the roster. A CRM pops. GenAI Studio may draft a summary. E911 carries a location. Reports leave through a role and an API.

docs.ti: Workforce, quality, and the recording shelf
docs.ex: Workforce, quality, and the recording shelf. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Five9 says it manages install and upgrades for the solution it delivers. The data sheet is the short version of that claim.

docs.ex: Analytics and the report that is not a dashboard rumor. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Analytics shows up on the WEM page and inside reporting. They are not one button. Standard reports need the Reporting role. Categories include ACD Queue, Campaign, Call Log, and the rest of that list. Layouts are tabular, summary, and matrix.

docs.ti: AI agents are a handoff with a name
docs.ex: AI agents are a handoff with a name. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Five9 Engage talks about self-service and the agent desktop together. Studio holds a digital IVA task. GenAI Studio is where knowledge and prompts are tested, and the product page says it powers Five9 AI applications, starting with Agent Assist summaries. This lab does not name a default model.

docs.ti: CRM, UC, and the desktop are three contracts
docs.ex: CRM, UC, and the desktop are three contracts. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Plus adapters named in the technical requirements include Salesforce, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, Zendesk, Oracle, NetSuite, Epic, and the Agent Desktop Toolkit. docs.ti: The glossary is the contract with yourself
docs.ex: The glossary is the contract with yourself. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Teams lose hours to words that Five9 uses narrowly: domain, skill, campaign profile, DNIS, disposition, list penetration, vertical dialing, campaign, autodial, blended, manual touch. docs.ex: Read the map before you add a box. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. Integration maps fail when a logo is enough. Salesforce in the IVR is a module. Salesforce on the desktop is an adapter. Certified Caller is not the ANI. RedSky is not the ITSP. Verint is not automatically your WEM. Studio regions are not Equinix edges.

docs.ex: University is a catalog, not a secret exam code. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ex: Practice is the domain, not the badge. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. docs.ex: How to answer without inventing. Source check 2026-10; unconfirmed if the vendor page moved. An interview answer in this lab has four beats: the object, the behavior, the page, and the gap.
